name: Preserve explicit Goal transfers during background sync

current_round.prompt:
Outcome: keep a Goal on the node selected by its latest unambiguous explicit transfer while preserving Refine background state-sync error reconciliation.

User intent: Goals move between nodes only through supported transfer surfaces such as the CLI or web UI. When one side changed node_id from the merge base and the other side did not, that one-sided transfer is authoritative and every node must converge to the transferred node. Background sync must never repatriate the Goal to its merge-base owner merely because a conflict occurred.

Scope and constraints:
1. Keep the background post-conflict recovery/reconciliation pipeline. Do not remove or disable attempt_automatic_state_recovery, state_sync_auto_recovery, its stored setting and web control, health/backoff settlement, recovery activity evidence, explicit sync authority, or useful automatic reconciliation for non-ownership conflicts.
2. Narrow or replace only the ownership decision that lets merge-base ownership reverse an explicit transfer. Do not use timestamps, current host, merge location, retry order, or merge-base ownership as a substitute for an explicit transfer.
3. Preserve a provable one-sided transferred node_id through deterministic resolution, agent-assisted resolution, and any later automatic recovery fallback, including when other fields in the same Goal record conflict. If whole-record authority cannot preserve that field safely, introduce the smallest field-aware policy or path handling needed; do not solve it by making every background conflict manual.
4. If both sides independently changed node_id to different nodes, or operands are missing or malformed such that a one-sided transfer cannot be proven, fail closed with stable conflict and health evidence and a domain-terms decision resolvable through existing supported sync-authority or Goal-transfer surfaces. Never delete a Goal or change node_id from ambiguous evidence.
5. Preserve all non-ownership background reconciliation, retained refs, crash/race safety, explicit operator recovery, and audit evidence.

Historical evidence: cancelled Goal DR427BFD89E5391018EACA69CC over-expanded this request. Its Round 1 candidate removed the automatic recovery branch, setting, activity contract, tests, and documentation; its generated Round 2 explicitly prohibited restoring them. Those removals are rejected requirements and must not be carried onto main. The useful ownership-gate idea may be reconsidered only if adapted to coexist with background recovery. Preserve that cancelled Goal, its two Rounds, branches, candidates, worktrees, logs, and Quality evidence unchanged.

Verification and evidence:
- Add focused tests for one-sided transfers in both local and remote orientations, with simultaneous non-owner field conflicts, and prove the final node_id is the transferred node.
- Cover competing transfers, missing/deleted/malformed peer operands, agent output that attempts the prior owner or deletion, and prove ambiguous cases remain unchanged and inspectable until explicit recovery.
- Prove ordinary non-ownership background conflicts still enter automatic recovery and retain health, backoff, activity, setting, and retained-state contracts.
- Run focused persistence-sync resolution/state, worker/config, sync simulation/regression, and relevant web tests; cargo fmt --all -- --check; git diff --check; scoped Clippy or repository-valid baseline handling. Report exact commands, results, candidate commit, base commit, and changed paths.

goal.name: Preserve explicit Goal transfers during background sync

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.
guidance_candidates.name: Intent and architecture
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
guidance_candidates.name: Cohesive code files
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

agent_context.workflow_summary: Refine gives this Goal Agent an isolated worktree and a finalized implementation plan. Implement the current Round and report evidence; a separate agent will review and correct the candidate in Quality, then an independent Governance gate will verify policy and integrate the exact passing commit before human Review. Do not directly advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

findings.description: The checklist contains no implementation item for the authoritative request's focused transfer, ambiguity, malformed/deleted operand, hostile agent output, ordinary auto-recovery, simulation, web, formatting, Clippy, or exact commit and path evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add a verification and evidence checklist item covering every required matrix case and exact repository-valid commands, results, base, candidate commit, and changed paths.

findings.description: P4 scopes the field-aware safeguard to automatic fallback even though CLI and API authority use the same recovery path, and it does not require reclassification from the freshly pinned operands on each bounded retry rather than reusing a stale report-derived decision.
findings.recommendation: Enforce ownership centrally for every decision-based recovery pass and recompute it from that pass's actual merge base, local head, and remote head before publication.

findings.description: P3 strengthens the agent acceptance gate but omits the existing crash-only surviving-result shortcut, which publishes a previously gated result ref without invoking the gate and could therefore publish deletion or prior ownership after the policy changes.
findings.recommendation: Revalidate surviving resolution results against the pinned ownership classification before publication, retiring and re-deriving any result that violates the transfer or ambiguity policy.

result.summary: The plan captures the core ownership rule but needs three safety-critical additions before implementation.

checklist.description: Add one cohesive Goal-ownership policy within application persistence sync that parses and validates the actual merge-base, local, and remote Goal operands and classifies ownership as unchanged, one valid one-sided transfer with its authoritative node_id, or ambiguity caused by competing transfers, missing or deleted peers, malformed records, or invalid node identifiers without using timestamps, host identity, merge location, retry order, or merge-base ownership as authority.

Invoke that policy centrally for every deterministic, agent-assisted, automatic, CLI-authorized, and API-authorized decision-based recovery pass, recomputing the classification from the freshly pinned merge base, local head, and remote head on every bounded retry before any result is published.

Apply the classification at the structural Goal merge boundary so a proven transferred node_id survives simultaneous non-owner field reconciliation in either local or remote orientation while an ambiguous ownership record remains contested and cannot be replaced or deleted.

Carry the pinned ownership classification into agent prompting and deterministic result acceptance so a proven transfer rejects deletion, the prior owner, or any different node_id and ambiguous ownership rejects any agent-selected ownership outcome.

Revalidate every crash-surviving agent resolution result against the current pass's freshly pinned ownership classification before publication, retiring and re-deriving a stale or violating result through the normal bounded path.

Keep existing whole-record recovery authority for ordinary non-ownership conflicts but overlay a proven transferred node_id onto any selected Goal record before publication, and decline automatic publication only when ownership cannot be proven safe.

Represent ambiguous ownership with a stable domain-terms conflict and health decision that preserves the current durable Goal unchanged and inspectable until an operator explicitly chooses existing sync authority or performs a supported Goal transfer.

Preserve the automatic-recovery branch and setting, health and backoff settlement, activity evidence, retained refs, race and crash fences, explicit recovery surfaces, and normal non-ownership convergence, and update only the affected intent pages if their documented transfer or recovery contract changes.

Add focused coverage for local- and remote-oriented one-sided transfers with concurrent non-owner conflicts, competing transfers, missing, deleted, and malformed operands, hostile agent deletion or prior-owner output, crash-surviving results, and ordinary automatic recovery, then record the exact repository-valid persistence-sync, worker and config, sync simulation and regression, web, formatting, diff, and scoped Clippy commands and results together with the base commit, candidate commit, and changed paths.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P9 now covers every required transfer, ambiguity, malformed or deleted operand, hostile-agent, surviving-result, ordinary recovery, simulation, web, formatting, Clippy, commit, and changed-path evidence requirement.

P2 centralizes the ownership safeguard for automatic and explicit CLI or API recovery and requires reclassification from each retry's freshly pinned merge base, local head, and remote head before publication.

P5 requires crash-surviving resolution refs to pass the same fresh ownership validation before publication and retires and re-derives any result that would delete the Goal or violate proven or ambiguous ownership.

result.summary: Preserve each provable one-sided explicit Goal transfer by enforcing a small field-aware ownership policy across every persistence-sync resolution and recovery path, while leaving ambiguous ownership unchanged and inspectable and retaining automatic reconciliation for all safe non-ownership conflicts.

checklist.description: Add a cohesive Goal-ownership reconciliation policy under application persistence sync that classifies base, local, and remote operands as unchanged ownership, one valid one-sided transfer with its authoritative node, or ambiguity from competing changes, deletion, absence, malformed data, or invalid node identifiers without consulting timestamps, host identity, merge location, retry order, or merge-base ownership.

Apply the shared policy at the structural Goal merge boundary so a provable transferred node_id survives disjoint field merging while ownership ambiguity keeps the record contested instead of selecting or deleting it.

Carry the ownership classification and updated transfer doctrine into agent-assisted state resolution, and make its deterministic acceptance gate reject deletion, the prior owner, or any other node_id when a one-sided transfer is provable while preventing an agent from choosing between ambiguous ownership operands.

Extend automatic recovery with the smallest field-aware decision needed to retain its existing whole-record authority for non-ownership conflicts while overlaying a proven transferred node_id onto the selected Goal record before the merge commit is published.

Make ambiguous ownership produce a stable domain-terms decision in the existing conflict report and leave durable state unchanged and inspectable until the current sync-authority or Goal-transfer surfaces provide an explicit decision.

Keep the worker's attempt_automatic_state_recovery branch, opt-out setting, health and backoff settlement, retained refs, activity evidence, race fences, and ordinary automatic convergence intact, with the ownership policy declining only cases that cannot prove a safe transfer outcome.

Update the affected Fleet, persistence-sync, CLI, API, and runtime-setting intent text to describe explicit-transfer precedence, field-aware fallback, and fail-closed ambiguity without changing the established surface contracts.

result.summary: Change state reconciliation to carry a provable one-sided Goal transfer as field-level authority through deterministic merging, agent resolution, and automatic fallback, while keeping ambiguous ownership fail-closed and preserving background recovery for unrelated conflicts.
